newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $69 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $69 -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were slow near midday Thursday, with light trading at $69.00 per cwt reported, steady with Wednesday, feedlot sources said.
About 600 heifers that will likely grade select and choice sold in Kansas, USDA said.
This week's top price was $69.00 during Wednesday's active trade, which was $3.00 higher than last week's top.
Fed cattle next week were seen trading $1.00 higher at $70.00, buoyed by strong beef prices and tight supplies of finished cattle.
A few loads sold at $70.00 Wednesday in western Nebraska, which also fueled optimism for higher prices, sources said.

For the week, 112,900 head were confirmed by USDA sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area, including 20,900 formulated cattle and 800 previously contracted to be shipped this week and 300 head or eight loads of cattle to be delivered against Chicago Mercantile Exchange futures.
Kansas sales for the week to date, including Thursday morning, were estimated at 88,000 head, with 15,200 head or about 17 percent contracted or formulated cattle.
Beef prices at midday were quoted up $1.28 to $1.51 per cwt, with 151 fabricated loads sold, USDA said. Heavyweight choice beef was quoted up $1.28 at $105.90.
The heavyweight choice value has jumped $8.52 from Thursday's close last week, USDA statistics showed. It also was the highest level since Dec 31, 1996.
